text: Read beside the earlier promise, the chapter stands at less distance from it than at first appears. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed. The narrator recalls as much only to turn that promise into a test. Much depends upon a single word, _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham speaks three times in the scene. To be present, for him, is to lose. He gives the word once to God, once to Isaac, and once to the angel. It means something different at each answer, and each answer costs him more than the one before it.
